_comment: Multi-voter battery defense (v2). Source of truth for the sysfs-direct battery watchdog. Cross-checks BAT1 + ADP1 + sample-history + wall-clock so a SAM data-path freeze cannot prevent hibernation. ANY enabled voter with critical verdict triggers `systemctl <action_at_critical>` (OR-vote). v1 (single capacity check) failed on 2026-04-30: BAT1 sysfs was wedged at capacity=100 for 3.5h while the laptop drained to firmware power-off — no userspace work was saved. Consumed by `configuration_system-protection-battery.nix`.

watch._comment: battery_device + ac_device are sysfs power_supply names. poll_seconds is the systemd OnUnitActiveSec interval. state_dir holds rolling sample history + last-charging timestamp; created by systemd StateDirectory=. history_polls bounds the rolling window (also used by stuck_sam voter).

voters._comment: Each voter independently verdicts {ok, low, critical}. Disabled voters are skipped at evaluation time (no fallback). Designed for OR-vote: ANY critical → action.

bat_capacity._comment: Original v1 check. Kernel-derived integer 0..100. Trusts SAM. PRIMARY trigger: hibernate at critical_pct (owner requirement 2026-06-13: hibernation happens at 15% ONLY; above that the energy plan only locks/screensaves on idle). low_pct drives the advisory low-battery notification, no action.

bat_energy_ratio._comment: Computes ratio from raw energy_now / energy_full µWh. Catches off-by-rounding cases the integer capacity field misses. Same SAM root as capacity, so freezes together — useful only against integer-rounding edge cases, not against full SAM freeze. Critical matches bat_capacity (15%).

voltage_under_min._comment: DISABLED 2026-05-07 — false positives on Surface Pro 8: voltage_now dips below voltage_min_design under transient load even at 60-90% SoC, triggering a hibernate loop (boot -1 fired at cap=63 / vnow=11.323V / vmin_design ~ 11.4V). Assumption that voltage<voltage_min_design ⇒ empty does not hold for SP8 cells. Other voters (capacity, energy_ratio, alarm, adp_offline_time, stuck_sam) cover the original failure modes without this false-positive vector. Re-enable only with margin_uV calibrated to observed SP8 sag depth + a require_capacity_below floor.

firmware_alarm._comment: ACPI/SAM alarm field non-zero means firmware itself crossed its low-battery threshold. Should fire well before deep discharge if firmware is healthy.

adp_offline_time._comment: Wall-clock fail-safe, CAPACITY-GATED. Fires only when AC has been offline ≥ max_minutes_off_ac AND capacity ≤ require_capacity_below. 2026-06-13 INCIDENT: ungated, this hibernated at 100% the instant AC was unplugged — the last_charging anchor had gone stale because a full plugged-in Surface reports status='Not charging' (anchor-reset bug, fixed in the .nix to reset on ADP1/online=1). The capacity gate is the second guard: a healthy charge can never trip a wall-clock timer. require_capacity_below must be ≥ bat_capacity.critical_pct so this only ever acts as a backstop near the real critical level.

stuck_sam._comment: SAM-freeze detector, CAPACITY-GATED. Triggers when the last min_static_polls samples show {capacity, energy_now, voltage_now} all unchanged AND an on-battery indicator was seen AND capacity ≤ require_capacity_below. The capacity gate (2026-06-13) stops a quiescent FULL battery on a brief unplug from reading as 'stuck + on-battery' and hibernating at 100%. Residual: a gauge frozen HIGH while truly draining is no longer caught — accepted per owner's 'hibernate at low battery ONLY'.

policy._comment: Voters are OR-ed (vote_logic=any). action_at_critical is a systemctl verb. Allowed: hibernate, suspend-then-hibernate, hybrid-sleep, poweroff (suspend verbs are banned by cloud-data-power.json actions.never — Surface S3 is broken). Default `hibernate` requires `resume=` on kernel cmdline and a swap area ≥ /sys/power/image_size on a non-zram backing device.
policy._fallback_comment: 2026-06-12 incident: the swapfile was unreachable (p5 superblock destroyed), every `systemctl hibernate` failed with 'Not enough suitable swap space', and the watchdog just retried each poll until the battery hit physical 0% and the firmware power-cut. With this policy the watchdog counts consecutive FAILED critical actions (state file action_failures); after max_action_failures it escalates to action_at_critical_fallback. poweroff loses the RAM session but is a clean filesystem shutdown — strictly better than a firmware power-cut. The counter resets on any poll that is not critical and on any successful action.

testers._comment: One invariant per voter input + infra invariants. Wire into reports-logs or a dedicated CI job.

checks.description: battery-watchdog.timer is active
battery-watchdog.service is loaded (timer-driven oneshot)
BAT1/capacity returns an integer 0..100 (voter: bat_capacity)
BAT1/status returns a known state (voters: bat_capacity, bat_energy_ratio, voltage_under_min, stuck_sam)
BAT1/energy_now returns a non-negative integer µWh (voter: bat_energy_ratio, stuck_sam)
BAT1/energy_full returns a positive integer µWh (voter: bat_energy_ratio)
BAT1/voltage_now returns a non-negative integer µV (voter: voltage_under_min, stuck_sam)
BAT1/voltage_min_design returns a positive integer µV (voter: voltage_under_min)
BAT1/alarm returns an integer (voter: firmware_alarm)
ADP1/online returns 0 or 1 (voter: adp_offline_time, stuck_sam)
StateDirectory created and writable (voters: adp_offline_time, stuck_sam)
Rolling sample history file present after first run (voter: stuck_sam)
Kernel cmdline has resume= so hibernation can resume on next boot
logind reports hibernate is permitted (CanHibernate is a logind D-Bus property, NOT a systemctl-show property — `systemctl show -p CanHibernate` silently prints nothing)
checks.command: busctl call org.freedesktop.login1 /org/freedesktop/login1 org.freedesktop.login1.Manager CanHibernate | awk '{gsub(/"/,""); print $2}'

checks.description: Kernel has a resume device registered (/sys/power/resume != 0:0) — without it hibernate entry fails even with healthy swap (2026-06-12: device appeared after boot, devno never registered, CanHibernate=na)
The non-zram swapfile is active swap (2026-06-12: only zram was active — zram cannot back hibernation)
Disk swap (non-zram) ≥ /sys/power/image_size budget
deployed battery-watchdog hibernates bat_capacity at 15% (owner 2026-06-13: hibernate at 15% ONLY)
REGRESSION GUARD (hibernate-at-100% 2026-06-13): adp_offline_time + stuck_sam are capacity-gated in the deployed watchdog, so a wall-clock/stuck voter can never fire on a healthy charge
REGRESSION GUARD: last_charging anchor resets on ADP1/online=1 (not only Charging/Full), so unplugging a full battery starts a fresh off-AC clock instead of an instant stale-anchor trip
